judgment: If local systems report unauthorized headings, decide case-by-case whether creating an authority record is justified locally to support heading control and file integrity, since software cannot treat the CONSER bib as an authority.
resolution: Create an authority record for the serial’s preferred title when local policy/system needs require controlled headings (especially when the heading is used in subjects/added entries elsewhere).
transferable_pattern: When your system requires authority control and flags serial headings justified only by bib records, resolve by creating the needed authority record locally to enable automated validation and reduce manual heading maintenance.
field_hint: Authority records (NACO SAR); bib 130 and related access points
evidence_quote: "if your ILS reporting system spits out reports of unauthorized headings... you’ll need to consider at that time if an authority record is justified"
_judge_reason: It describes a real recurring workflow problem (ILS flags unauthorized headings justified only by CONSER bib 130), requires local judgment about whether authority control is worth it, and resolves with the concrete action of creating a local/NACO authority record—a pattern applicable across different serials/newspapers.

problem: A serial/continuing resource title changes because a gendered word in the title shifts (e.g., maire ↔ mairesse) after an election, and the cataloger must decide whether this is a major or minor title change.
judgment: Treat the change as grammatical inflection (gender as a type of inflection) and therefore a minor change rather than a new work/record situation.
resolution: Do not create a new bibliographic record for a major title change; instead treat it as a minor title change and update/record the variant title on the existing record (e.g., add a variant title note/field).
transferable_pattern: When a title varies only by grammatical inflection (including gendered forms) with the same root word, handle it as a minor title change and record the variant on the existing serial record rather than starting a new record.
evidence_quote: "I would consider this a change in grammatical form, which is a minor change under RDA 2.3.2.13.2."
_judge_reason: It describes a real recurring cataloging situation (gendered inflection in serial titles), makes a judgment call about major vs minor change, and gives an actionable resolution (keep the same record and add a variant title) that would apply to other newspapers.

problem: A serial title conflicts with other serials of the same title in the catalog, making it hard to distinguish and control access.
judgment: When there are multiple serials with the same title, create a preferred title with a qualifier to disambiguate.
resolution: Create a 130 preferred title and add a parenthetical qualifier (e.g., place) to differentiate the serial.
transferable_pattern: If a newspaper/serial title is non-unique in your catalog, establish a qualified preferred title (130) to disambiguate it from other identically titled serials.
evidence_quote: "I created a 130 when I cataloged a newspaper titled Ensign because there were several Ensigns in the catalog. In this instance, I added a qualifier  Ensign (Nephi,Utah)."
_judge_reason: It describes a real recurring ambiguity problem (non-unique serial titles), requires cataloger judgment about adding an appropriate qualifier, and resolves it via a concrete action (creating a 130 with a parenthetical qualifier) that generalizes to other newspapers.

problem: Local systems/ILS authority-control reports flag serial headings as unauthorized because the authorized access point is justified by a CONSER bibliographic record rather than a separate authority record, and software may not treat CONSER bib records as authority sources.
judgment: Decide institutionally whether creating an authority record is justified to satisfy local authority-control workflows, especially when headings are needed in subject/added entries for other works.
resolution: Either (a) rely on the CONSER record as justification and accept/manual-handle the unauthorized-heading reports, or (b) create an authority record locally when needed to support system control/reporting.
transferable_pattern: When your system can’t authority-control serial AAPs justified only by CONSER bib records, choose between manual maintenance vs. creating local authority records based on your institution’s reporting/control needs.
evidence_quote: "if your ILS reporting system spits out reports of unauthorized headings, it will contain such cases where a CONSER record was used to justify a heading in lieu of using staff time to create an authority record. Depending on your institution's policies, you'll need to consider at that time if an authority record is justified at your institution."
_judge_reason: It describes a real recurring workflow problem with ILS authority-control reports, requires an institutional decision, and offers actionable resolution options that generalize to other newspapers/systems facing CONSER-justified headings without authority records.

problem: Catalogers need to know what form of authorized access point to use for a serial when no separate authority record exists, and the serial’s CONSER record may have different combinations of 130/1XX/240/245.
judgment: Use the CONSER record as the authority surrogate: prefer 130 if present; otherwise use 1XX+240/245; if no 1XX, use 245 as the access point.
resolution: Construct the access point for related works/subject entries by copying the appropriate form from the CONSER bib record (130, or 1XX+240/245, or 245 alone).
transferable_pattern: When no authority record exists for a serial, derive the authorized access point consistently from the CONSER bibliographic record’s 130/1XX/240/245 configuration.
evidence_quote: "If the CONSER record has a 130, use that. If it has another 1XX field, use that plus the 240 (if present) or 245. If there is no 1XX field, the 245 serves as the access point."
_judge_reason: It describes a real recurring cataloging situation (no authority record), requires choosing among bib-field configurations, and gives an actionable, reusable procedure for constructing access points from the CONSER record that would apply to other serials.

problem: Catalogers are unsure whether they can start using a newly validated MARC field (023) in CONSER-authenticated records after a WorldCat validation update.
judgment: Rely on CONSER acceptability/authorization rather than local/system validation alone; confirmation from the ISSN/CONSER authorities determines whether the field may be used in CONSER records.
resolution: Begin using field 023 in CONSER-authenticated records for ISSN-L once confirmed as valid/allowed (as stated), rather than waiting solely on validation changes.
transferable_pattern: When a cataloging network adds validation for a field, confirm policy/authorization for the record type (e.g., CONSER-authenticated) before changing practice, then implement the field consistently.
evidence_quote: "With the 8/26 update to WorldCat validation, now including 023, I'm wondering if we're any closer to using the field in CONSER-authenticated records?"
_judge_reason: It describes a real workflow problem triggered by a system change, requires a policy-based judgment beyond mere validation, and resolves with a concrete practice (use 023 once CONSER/ISSN authorities confirm) that generalizes to other fields and newspapers.

problem: OCLC is about to bulk-move ISSN-L data from deprecated fields into a new field, raising the risk of duplicate/conflicting data entry during the transition.
judgment: Avoid treating the transition as a change in meaning; expect automated remediation and coordinate timing to prevent redundant manual edits or inconsistent placement.
resolution: Allow/anticipate OCLC’s process to move ISSN-L from 022 $l/$m to 023; during the transition, place new ISSN-L in 023 and monitor for further instructions about the migration process.
transferable_pattern: During vendor/network field migrations, enter new data in the target field and plan for automated backfile conversion to reduce duplication and inconsistency.
evidence_quote: "In the coming weeks, OCLC will begin moving ISSN-L data from deprecated fields 022 $l and $m into field 023."
_judge_reason: It describes a real transition problem (risk of duplicate/conflicting ISSN-L entries), requires judgment about timing and meaning during migration, and resolves with a concrete practice (enter in 023 and rely on/monitor automated conversion) that generalizes to other vendor/network field migrations.
